accepted.s: Who identified eight centres of origin of cultivated plants?
accepted.x: N. I. Vavilov identified eight centres of origin of cultivated plants.
accepted.tq: Use direct person–contribution recall.
accepted.sec: Agro-biodiversity - Vavilov centres, crop wild relatives

accepted.s: Which of the following crop combinations is associated with the Hindustan (Indo-Burma) centre of origin?
o: Rice, sugarcane, mango, pigeon pea, brinjal, cucumber and black pepper
Wheat, barley, olive, grape and cabbage
accepted.x: The Hindustan or Indian centre is associated with rice, sugarcane, mango, pigeon pea, brinjal, cucumber and black pepper. It is also associated with many pulses and citrus.
accepted.tq: Match a named centre with its characteristic crop group.
accepted.sec: Agro-biodiversity - Vavilov centres, crop wild relatives

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s cultivated crops and crop wild relatives:
1. India has 811 cultivated crop species.
2. India has 902 crop wild relatives.
3. Crop wild relatives have no significance for crop improvement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India has 811 cultivated crop species and 902 crop wild relatives. Statement 3 is false because crop wild relatives can provide useful traits for crop improvement and resilience.
accepted.tq: Split the numerical statements from the extreme negative statement.
accepted.sec: Agro-biodiversity - Vavilov centres, crop wild relatives

accepted.s: Borjuli wetland Biodiversity Heritage Site in Assam protects which crop wild relative?
accepted.x: Borjuli wetland protects Oryza rufipogon, the wild ancestor or progenitor of cultivated rice, Oryza sativa.
accepted.tq: Use exact scientific-name discrimination.
accepted.sec: Agro-biodiversity - Vavilov centres, crop wild relatives

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a significant adaptive feature of Oryza rufipogon mentioned in relation to crop biodiversity?
o: Complete immunity to all fungal diseases
Resistance to pests and tolerance of floods and salinity
Tolerance only to severe frost and snow
Ability to grow exclusively in arid deserts
accepted.x: Oryza rufipogon is noted for pest resistance and tolerance of floods and salinity, making it valuable as a crop wild relative.
accepted.tq: Apply the ecological traits of a wild relative to its conservation value.
accepted.sec: Agro-biodiversity - Vavilov centres, crop wild relatives

accepted.s: India’s Citrus Gene Sanctuary is located in which of the following places?
o: Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary, Andhra Pradesh
Nokrek Biosphere Reserve, Garo Hills, Meghalaya
accepted.x: India’s Citrus Gene Sanctuary is located in the Nokrek Biosphere Reserve in the Garo Hills of Meghalaya.
accepted.tq: Test precise location rather than the broader region.
accepted.sec: Agro-biodiversity - Vavilov centres, crop wild relatives

accepted.s: The Eastern Ghats extend approximately from the—
o: Godavari delta to the Aravalli Hills
Ganga delta to the Gulf of Kachchh
Narmada valley to the Nilgiri Hills
accepted.x: The Eastern Ghats run from the Mahanadi delta in the north to Kanyakumari in the south.
accepted.tq: Use endpoint-based geographical recall.
accepted.sec: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the vegetation of the Eastern Ghats?
o: Deciduous, semi-evergreen and evergreen forests, together with savanna, scrub and estuarine vegetation
Only mangrove forests and coral reefs
Only alpine grasslands and coniferous forests
accepted.x: The Eastern Ghats contain deciduous, semi-evergreen and evergreen forests, along with savanna, scrub and estuarine vegetation.
accepted.tq: Choose the most complete ecological description.
accepted.sec: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

accepted.s: Arma Konda, the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats, has an elevation of approximately—
accepted.x: Arma Konda is the highest peak of the Eastern Ghats and rises to about 1,680 metres. It is located in Alluri Sitharama Raju district.
accepted.tq: Test a precise figure with closely spaced numerical options.
accepted.sec: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Seshachalam hills is correct?
1. Red Sanders occurs naturally only in the Seshachalam region.
2. Cycas beddomei is a rare endemic cycad of the hills.
3. The Golden Gecko is a micro-endemic fauna of the region.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Red Sanders, Cycas beddomei and the Golden Gecko are all characteristic biodiversity elements of the Seshachalam hills. The Golden Gecko is described as micro-endemic.
accepted.tq: When all three statements are independently supported, select the complete combination.
accepted.sec: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Seshachalam — Natural habitat of Red Sanders
Arma Konda — Highest peak of the Eastern Ghats
Coringa — Second-largest mangrove ecosystem in India
Mahendra Girulu — Hills of the Anantapur region
accepted.x: Mahendra Girulu is the name used for the Eastern Ghats hills in Srikakulam. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the location mismatch among closely related regional facts.
accepted.sec: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

accepted.s: Coringa in Kakinada is described as India’s—
accepted.x: Coringa in Kakinada is India’s second-largest mangrove ecosystem.
accepted.tq: Test a size-ranking fact with ecological distractors.
accepted.sec: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding biodiversity conservation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve was notified in 2010.
2. The Seshachalam and Nallamala corridors support tigers, leopards and elephants.
3. Chenchus are associated with these Eastern Ghats landscapes as a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve was notified in 2010, the corridors support major mammals, and the Chenchus are a PVTG living in the landscape.
accepted.tq: Combine date, habitat and community facts in a coded statement question.
accepted.sec: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Eastern Ghats is correct?
o: They have no recognised biodiversity significance in India.
They are not among the 36 global biodiversity hotspots, although some descriptions call them a biodiversity hotspot.
They are included among all 36 global biodiversity hotspots.
They are a continuous range without any scrub or savanna vegetation.
accepted.x: Some descriptions call the Eastern Ghats a biodiversity hotspot, but they are not included among the 36 global biodiversity hotspots.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a descriptive label from formal global classification.
accepted.sec: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board works through approximately how many Biodiversity Management Committees?
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board works through about 13,000 Biodiversity Management Committees and People's Biodiversity Registers.
accepted.tq: Use place-value discrimination for an institutional figure.
accepted.sec: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

accepted.s:
Which of the following is associated with the Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board?
1. Sharing 5% of Red Sanders sale profits with farmers.
2. Preparing a Marine Access and Benefit Sharing framework for fishers.
3. Working through People’s Biodiversity Registers.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Board shares 5% of Red Sanders sale profits with farmers, works through People's Biodiversity Registers and is preparing a Marine ABS framework for fishers.
accepted.tq: Test an institutional body through its functions and mechanisms.
accepted.sec: AP biodiversity - Eastern Ghats and Seshachalam

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Species)
a. Red Sanders
b. Golden Gecko
c. Jerdon’s Courser
d. Slender Loris

List-II (Habitat in Andhra Pradesh)
i. Dry scrub forests
 ii. Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary, Kadapa
 iii. Seshachalam, Veligonda and Nallamala hills
 iv. Seshachalam Eastern Ghats micro-habitats

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Red Sanders occurs in the Seshachalam, Veligonda and Nallamala hills; Golden Gecko in Seshachalam micro-habitats; Jerdon’s Courser in Sri Lankamalleswara WLS; and Slender Loris in dry scrub forests.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure habitat pair and eliminate codes.
accepted.sec: Endemic species of AP - habitat  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Jerdon’s Courser is correctly described as a—
o: critically endangered and nocturnal species of Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary
accepted.x: Jerdon’s Courser is critically endangered and nocturnal, and its Andhra Pradesh habitat is Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary in Kadapa.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among species using status, behaviour and habitat.
accepted.sec: Endemic species of AP - habitat  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Andhra Pradesh’s state tree and Red Sanders?
o: Golden Gecko is the state tree of Andhra Pradesh.
Cycas beddomei is the state tree of Andhra Pradesh.
Neem is the state tree of Andhra Pradesh; Red Sanders is not the state tree.
Red Sanders is officially the state tree of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.x: Neem is the state tree of Andhra Pradesh. Red Sanders is not the state tree, despite appearing as such in one list.
accepted.tq: Resolve a conflicting label using the precise official distinction.
accepted.sec: Endemic species of AP - habitat  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly represents the estimates of described species and total living species?
1. About 1.5 million living species have been described.
2. About 300,000 fossil species have been described.
3. E. O. Wilson estimated the total number of living species at 10–50 million.
4. Robert May’s estimate was about 7 million living species.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four estimates are stated figures: about 1.5 million described living species, 300,000 described fossil species, Wilson’s 10–50 million estimate and May’s estimate of about 7 million.
accepted.tq: Separate multiple numerical estimates and retain the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Species estimates and the largest taxonomic groups  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the taxonomic composition of recorded species is correct?
o: Animals constitute over 70% of recorded species, plants account for about 22%, and insects are the richest animal group.
Plants constitute over 70% of all recorded species.
Insects constitute less than 1% of recorded animal species.
Animals and plants each constitute approximately 50% of recorded species.
accepted.x: Over 70% of recorded species are animals, plants account for about 22%, and insects are the richest group among animals.
accepted.tq: Use relative shares and the within-group comparison together.
accepted.sec: Species estimates and the largest taxonomic groups  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the cited 2026 record, India has approximately how many bat species, including how many endemic species?
accepted.x: The cited record lists about 135 bat species in India, of which 16 are endemic.
accepted.tq: Test a paired count with a closely related numerical distractor.
accepted.sec: Species estimates and the largest taxonomic groups  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Genetic diversity primarily refers to—
o: the number of species in a geographical area
the number of ecological roles in a food web
variation among ecosystems in different climatic regions
accepted.x: Genetic diversity is variation within a species and is the basic source of biodiversity. Different varieties of Oryza sativa illustrate this level.
accepted.tq: Test the exact level-to-definition relationship.
accepted.sec: Levels - genetic, species, ecosystem diversity  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: All rice varieties may belong to Oryza sativa but differ in size, aroma and nutrients. This is an example of—
accepted.x: Differences among varieties of the same species represent genetic diversity.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition to a concrete biological example.
accepted.sec: Levels - genetic, species, ecosystem diversity  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes species diversity?
o: The variety of climatic zones on Earth
Variation in genes within a single species only
Only the number of species in an area, irrespective of their abundance
The variety of species in an area, involving richness as well as abundance
accepted.x: Species diversity concerns the variety of species in an area and includes both species richness and abundance.
accepted.tq: Distinguish species diversity from the narrower concept of richness.
accepted.sec: Levels - genetic, species, ecosystem diversity  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about ecosystem diversity:
1. It refers to the variety of ecosystems such as rainforests, deciduous forests and boreal ecosystems.
2. One ecosystem can always replace the functions of another ecosystem.
3. Boreal conifers cannot perform the same ecological role as tropical deciduous trees in every context.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is false because one ecosystem cannot simply replace another; boreal conifers cannot do the job of tropical deciduous trees in every context.
accepted.tq: Use the absolute word in the replacement claim as the false-statement trap.
accepted.sec: Levels - genetic, species, ecosystem diversity  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Forest A contains 2 tigers, 6 deer and 7 rabbits, while Forest B contains 1 tiger, 6 deer and 8 rabbits. Which conclusion is correct?
o: Forest B is more even because it has more rabbits.
Forest A has greater species richness and Forest B has greater ecosystem diversity.
Forest A and Forest B differ in species richness but not in evenness.
Both forests have three species and 15 individuals, but Forest A is more even.
accepted.x: Both forests contain three species and 15 individuals. Forest A has a more equal distribution of individuals and is therefore more even.
accepted.tq: Separate richness from the distribution of individuals.
accepted.sec: Species richness vs evenness; diversity indices  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes species richness from species evenness?
o: Richness is the number of species, whereas evenness is how equally individuals are distributed among those species.
Richness refers to genetic variation, whereas evenness refers to fossil diversity.
Richness is the abundance of the dominant species, whereas evenness is the total number of ecosystems.
Richness and evenness are two names for the same measure.
accepted.x: Species richness is the number of species present, while species evenness indicates how equally individuals are distributed among them.
accepted.tq: Test a commonly confused pair through contrasting definitions.
accepted.sec: Species richness vs evenness; diversity indices  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following indices are used to measure biodiversity?
1. Shannon-Wiener index
2. Simpson index
3. Vavilov index
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Shannon-Wiener and Simpson are biodiversity indices. Vavilov is associated with centres of origin of cultivated plants, not a biodiversity index.
accepted.tq: Separate measurement indices from an unrelated named concept.
accepted.sec: Species richness vs evenness; diversity indices  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Functional diversity is primarily concerned with—
o: the number of crop species cultivated by humans
the range of ecological roles performed by organisms
only the number of fossil species in a region
the geographical extent of a biosphere reserve
accepted.x: Functional diversity measures the range of ecological roles. Its components include functional richness, functional evenness and functional divergence.
accepted.tq: Link a term with its defining ecological function.
accepted.sec: Species richness vs evenness; diversity indices  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Component of functional diversity)
a. Functional richness
b. Functional evenness
c. Functional divergence

List-II (Meaning)
i. Dominance of extreme traits
 ii. Range of niches occupied
 iii. Spread of abundance across niches

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Functional richness refers to the niches occupied, functional evenness to the spread of abundance across niches, and functional divergence to the dominance of extreme traits.
accepted.tq: Start with the direct definition of richness and eliminate the remaining codes.
accepted.sec: Species richness vs evenness; diversity indices  [GROUP-II]
